title: Unit – 4 : Session – 9 : SLO – 2  |  TCP and UDP Socket Types
sections: 1. TCP — Reliable, ordered: connection-oriented byte stream with acknowledgements, retransmission and sequencing.
2. UDP — Fast, no guarantee: connectionless datagrams with no delivery or ordering guarantee, minimal overhead.
3. Port — Logical communication endpoint: a 16-bit number identifying a specific process/service on a host.
TCP use cases: web (HTTP/HTTPS), email, file transfer — where correctness matters.
UDP use cases: live video/voice, DNS, online gaming — where speed matters more than perfection.
A socket = IP address + port + protocol; TCP sockets are SOCK_STREAM, UDP sockets are SOCK_DGRAM.
